text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ten people were injured, one seriously, when a hotel ceiling collapsed on them while attending a business workshop organised by the Malawi Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA).
- The United Nations Population Fund has pledged about $15-million (Malawi Kwacha 228-million) for Malawi's 5-year health and population control programmes to begin next January.
- A tea estate in northern Malawi expected to lose $6,779 (MK101,690) in production after workers stopped watering tea shrubs due to a misunderstanding.
- Blantyre Water Board staff last Friday began an indefinite strike demanding a 200 percent salary increase.
- Zimbabwe Police recently arrested a truck driver at Nyamapanda after detecting an undisclosed consignment of marijuana in a truck from Malawi to Harare.

- The German government is prepared to release funds for establishing Malawi's second broadcast channel as the ruling United Democratic Front government is monopolising the only radio station in the country.
- An outbreak of rabies in Lilongwe, the Malawi capital has killed 12 people, raising the number to 23 from 11 last week.
